solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Superior to 9, mainly

definitions.meaning: 9 across is EVERYONE, so this means higher than every single person

explanation.surface: Someone is, for the most part, better than everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference to 9 must be filled in first: being superior to everyone is to be placed over the lot of them.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for 'chiefly', and read literally it means placed higher than every other person.

clue.text: Reluctant amateur's line of 29s?

parts.note: 29 across is DACTYL, and a line of dactyls is a line of poetry, verse

explanation.surface: An amateur poet is unwilling to write dactylic lines.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that verse is only one example of what a line of dactyls makes.
explanation.definitionFit: Averse means opposed or disinclined, so unwilling to do something.

clue.text: Jerks perhaps held in solitary with no holds barred

indicators.note: the exercise letters are kept inside the word for solitary

parts.note: only, as in an only child, means solitary
physical jerks are exercises, an example of PE, physical education

explanation.surface: Idiots kept in solitary confinement with no restrictions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerks' looks like fools; British 'physical jerks' are keep-fit exercises, so PE.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with nothing held back is doing it frankly and without concealment.

clue.text: Land where pain enters hearts of men and settles

indicators.note: the word for pain goes in between those middle letters
the central letters of men and settles are taken

parts.note: gyp is British slang for pain, as in 'my knee is giving me gyp'

explanation.surface: A country where suffering gets into the hearts of men and stays.
explanation.walkthrough: The hearts of MEN and SETTLES are E and T, and GYP goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt is a country, and land is a common word for a nation.

clue.text: A bit of skill and ingenuity in dock …

indicators.note: only a portion of the words skill and ingenuity supplies the letters

explanation.surface: Some skill and ingenuity is needed when mooring a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to 6 down, but this clue is complete on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A landing is a jetty or quay where boats tie up, a place to dock.

clue.text: Our troops in Germany halting early by short tiny tree

indicators.note: stopping before the end, so the last letter of the army's abbreviation is dropped

parts.note: BAOR, the British Army of the Rhine, the British forces once stationed in Germany

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter of the word for tiny is lost

parts.note: a tiny thing is a baby one

explanation.surface: British soldiers in Germany stop marching beside a small tree.
explanation.walkthrough: BAOR, the British Army of the Rhine, was the name for British forces stationed in West Germany during the Cold War.
explanation.definitionFit: The baobab is an African tree famous for its massively swollen trunk.

clue.text: … with man spared flogging

indicators.note: beating, which knocks the letters of man spared out of order

explanation.surface: Continuing 4 down: in the dock, a man is spared a whipping.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipses make one sentence with 4 down, but this clue stands alone: 'with' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The & symbol stands for 'and', which in writing can mean along with or together with.

clue.text: Plant's young growth ailed badly

parts.note: a bud is a new shoot on a plant

indicators.note: the letters of ailed are put into a poor, mixed-up order

explanation.surface: A plant's new shoots have been doing poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: Buddleia is a flowering shrub, the butterfly bush.

clue.text: Enclosure with a dry bar? Bring in last of Sauvignon and serve up!

indicators.note: an extra letter is introduced among the letters of a dry bar
the whole collection is dished out in a new arrangement
the final letter of the wine Sauvignon is taken

explanation.surface: A wine bar with no drink gets some Sauvignon delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: N, the last of Sauvignon, joins A DRY BAR, and 'serve up' rearranges all eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A barnyard is the fenced area around a farm's barn where animals are kept.

clue.text: The entire population's pretty identical, when seen after Ecstasy

indicators.note: the pieces for pretty and identical follow the letter for Ecstasy

parts.note: E is the drug slang abbreviation for ecstasy
pretty as in 'pretty good' means very
two things identical are one and the same

explanation.surface: Everyone looks attractive and alike once the drug has kicked in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pretty' looks like an adjective about looks, but it is the adverb VERY.
explanation.definitionFit: Everybody together makes up the whole of a population, a plain synonym phrase.

clue.text: Caught sight of 'Arriet, say, getting rest on the green

indicators.note: as one might say it, so the words are judged by their sound

parts.note: caught sight of her is 'spied her', and a Cockney like 'Arriet drops the H to give spied 'er

explanation.surface: Someone spots Harriet having a lie-down on the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys drop their H's (hence 'Arriet), so 'spied her' becomes 'spied 'er', which sounds like the answer. In snooker a spider is a raised cue rest used on the green baize.
explanation.definitionFit: In snooker a spider is a rest with tall legs that lets the cue pass over balls on the table's green cloth.

clue.text: Once, I was regularly in the paper

definitions.note: what is printed in a newspaper, a noun phrase for its content

indicators.note: every other letter of once I was is taken, starting with the second

explanation.surface: Someone recalls that they used to appear often in the press.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper is a vehicle for current reports of events, so the paper stands for its content.

clue.text: Stone rested within a rose I disturbed

indicators.note: one piece goes inside another
the letters of a rose I are stirred up into a new order

parts.note: a bird that rested on a branch lit on it

explanation.surface: A stone lay inside a rose that somebody knocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges A ROSE I into SOAIRE, and 'within' puts LIT inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A solitaire is a single gem, usually a diamond, set on its own in a ring.

clue.text: Place once again used for broadcast

definitions.meaning: to lay down a second time, as with a carpet or cable
to pass on a signal or programme

explanation.surface: A former venue is reused to transmit a programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place' reads as a noun, but it is a verb: to lay again.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay something afresh is to re-lay it, and to transmit a signal onwards is to relay it.

clue.text: Show off backing of costume …

indicators.note: the word for costume is taken from back to front

parts.note: garb is clothing or costume

explanation.surface: A performer flaunts the back of an outfit, with the next clue continuing the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: To brag is to boast, the verbal way of showing off.

clue.text: How to make cooks out of crooks instantly

definitions.text: How to make cooks out of crooks
definitions.meaning: crooks becomes cooks once its R, for right, is taken away

explanation.surface: Instructions for reforming criminals into chefs at once.
explanation.walkthrough: R is the standard abbreviation for right; taking it from CROOKS gives COOKS.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning immediately, at once.

clue.text: … wearing gaiters like an actor

indicators.note: something worn out has lost its shape, so the letters of gaiters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone in gaiters looks theatrical, carrying on from the show-off in the previous clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' reads as having on clothes, but it signals the letters of GAITERS being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagey means theatrical or exaggerated, so more stagey is more like a performer on stage.

clue.text: Setter's married — being weak!

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as I, so setter's is I'm, I am
a married couple is paired

explanation.surface: The setter confesses that marriage has made him feeble.
explanation.definitionFit: Impaired means damaged or weakened in function.

clue.text: It may help to recall — with rise of Medici, no men missed taking part

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters read upwards, so the hidden run is turned round
only part of the run Medici no men missed is used

explanation.surface: A historical aid to memory about the Medici rising with no men absent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise of' reverses the hidden letters CINOMENM, read upward in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A mnemonic is a memory aid such as a rhyme or acronym.

clue.text: Shifted flipping senior fellow

indicators.note: flipping over the phrase senior fellow puts its second word before its first

parts.note: a senior citizen is aged
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: An elderly man was moved, or someone swore at an old boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' swaps the order of the two words, not the letters: AGED MAN becomes MAN AGED.
explanation.definitionFit: To shift for oneself is to cope or get by, the same sense as to have coped.

clue.text: Immerse cloth in nothing

definitions.meaning: a heavy cotton or linen fabric used for sails and trousers
in cricket, a score of zero

explanation.surface: Dip a rag into nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition. A batsman out for no runs in cricket is out for a duck.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to plunge under water, a strong canvas-like fabric, and in cricket a score of zero.

clue.text: Old guitarist in a whirl

definitions.meaning: Duane ..., the American rock and roll guitarist of the 1950s and 60s
a swirl of water moving in a circle

explanation.surface: A veteran guitar player is in a spin.
explanation.definitionFit: Duane Eddy was a famous twanging guitarist, and a circular current in water is a little whirlpool.

clue.text: Girl regularly leaves untidy lettering in label

indicators.note: those letters depart from the fodder
the remaining letters are left in a messy new order
alternate letters of girl are taken, the first and third

explanation.surface: A girl keeps leaving messy writing on a tag.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd letters of GIRL are G and R; 'leaves' takes them from LETTERING, and 'untidy' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: To entitle is to give something a name or title, which is to label it.

clue.text: Top members of Edinburgh's National Chorus achieve marvellously perfect pitch

indicators.note: the first letter of each of the following words, the tops of a down entry

parts.words: Edinburgh's National Chorus achieve marvellously perfect

explanation.surface: Leading singers of a Scottish national choir hit the notes exactly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' means to set up camp, not a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: To pitch a tent is to set up camp, so the verb means to pitch.

clue.text: Butcher's poultry?

definitions.meaning: rhyming slang: butcher's hook means look
a male goose, one example of farm fowl

explanation.surface: A meat shop's poultry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butcher's' is British rhyming slang, butcher's hook for look; a gander is also a look.
explanation.definitionFit: A gander is a quick look, as is a butcher's, and it is also a male goose, a kind of poultry.

clue.text: Come clean in commercial with German

parts.note: an ad is a television commercial
mit is the German word for with

explanation.surface: Someone confesses during a German advert.
explanation.definitionFit: To confess or own up is to come clean, a common idiom.

clue.text: Security set-up arrests a nipper somewhere in Spain

indicators.note: holds, so the security body's letters go round the others

parts.note: the CIA, the US intelligence organisation
a talon is a claw that nips its prey

explanation.surface: Security services detain a young child somewhere in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nipper' looks like a small child; here it is a claw that nips.
explanation.definitionFit: Catalonia is the autonomous region in north-east Spain whose capital is Barcelona.

clue.text: Shed sheds mantle of autumn, slowly

indicators.note: a shed that sheds something casts it off like a coat, so one letter is dropped

parts.note: a lean-to is a shed built against a wall

indicators.note: the top of the word autumn, its covering first letter in a down entry

explanation.surface: A garden shed casts off its autumn covering, gently.
explanation.walkthrough: LEAN-TO sheds A, the first letter of autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: Lento is the musical direction for a slow tempo.

clue.text: Dud's leaving Down Under excitedly for stardom

indicators.note: the letters of dud depart from the fodder
the remaining letters of Down Under are thrown about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, three letters to remove

explanation.surface: A failure flies out of Australia in a state of excitement for fame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' removes D, U, D from DOWNUNDER, leaving OWNNER, and 'excitedly' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Renown is fame or celebrity, the state of being widely known as a star.

clue.text: Example shown by ace in one way and another

indicators.note: the letter for ace goes inside the string of road words

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
RD, the abbreviation for road, another kind of way
A is the card abbreviation for an ace

explanation.surface: An ace serves as a model in one way or another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in one way' tempts you to put the ace inside ST; it actually sits inside the second road, before its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a model or exemplar against which others are judged.

clue.text: Foot bill after daughter gets to Yale, oddly

indicators.note: the bill's letters come after the daughter's

parts.note: AC, the abbreviation for account, a bill to be settled

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of to Yale are kept

explanation.surface: A daughter is billed for her Ivy League studies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foot' means a metrical foot; the odd letters of TO YALE give TYL.
explanation.definitionFit: A dactyl is a metrical foot of one stressed then two unstressed syllables.

clue.text: Inferior to 28, and rather poorly

definitions.meaning: 28 across is STANDARD, so worse than the usual level

explanation.surface: Something not up to standard is feeling a bit under the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference to 28 must be filled in first; par is the expected standard in golf.
explanation.definitionFit: Par is the normal standard, so being under it means substandard, and the idiom also means slightly ill.
